meta.description: Machine-readable ledger tracking the migration of every production-reachable semantic type onto declarative manifests + recursive-ST4 assembly, per phase. Phase 1 (COMPLETE, frozen zero-debt gates): COBOL core + embedded SQL + embedded CICS. Phase 2 (active; queue order BMS_ARTIFACT first, FPAC second, one ledger item per worker): the BMS map-resource artifact pipeline and the FPac pipeline -- both are independent source/resource DSL pipelines, never COBOL dialects. Their parsing and semantics stay decoupled from COBOL; common rendering infrastructure is reused only where the semantic model genuinely supports it.

ratchet.note: Debt counts may only move down, per pipeline counter. Phase 1 counters (finalArchitectureCheck) are frozen at zero debt. Phase 2 counters live under ratchet.phase2 and are measured independently per scope.

cloudNativeGate.note: Full cloud-native gate is green. Initialized WORKING-STORAGE declarations are retained even when executable reachability marks them unused.

onlineCorpusInventory.note: Phase 3: inventory is now STATEMENT-ACCURATE (per source line+dialect+command, classified exactly once as PRESERVED / REJECTED / SILENT_DROP), no package-aggregate counting. DiagnosticSink (diagnostic.DiagnosticSink) collects structured diagnostics non-aborting so a whole program is inventoried per statement; throws when no sink is open (fail-closed gate). EXEC SQL INCLUDE counts as PRESERVED when it resolves/inlines (CJavaInline at the statement line).

rules: status may only advance forward along statusOrder
COBOL-scope direct backend count may only decrease (frozen at zero)
BMS (forms) direct backend count may only decrease
FPac direct backend count may only decrease
no unexplained allowlist may hide COBOL/SQL/CICS, BMS, or FPac debt
BMS entries must use scope BMS_ARTIFACT and FPac entries scope FPAC, never a COBOL dialect scope

phase2.note: Phase 2 baseline captured on top of commit 42d72b42 (the completed phase-1 HEAD). bmsDirectBackends counts generate/java/forms (incl. the CResourceStrings subclass); fpacDirectBackends counts generate/fpacjava (incl. the CSubStringAttributReference subclass). Each retirement slice tightens the matching checked-in Java inventory test (BmsFormsDirectBackendInventoryTest / FPacDirectBackendInventoryTest) and this counter together.

targetArchitecture.migrationPlaybook: 6 steps: (1) semantic entity read-only getters + de-abstract; (2) one semantic-*-bindings.properties line; (3) one java.stg template reading only entity.* properties; (4) feature-registry.yaml entry (+ runtime-operations.yaml/template-runtime-requirements.yaml if new runtime ops); (5) CJavaEntityFactoryST.NewEntity* override; (6) delete legacy direct backend + render test + ratchet bumps. READ domain (semantic.Verbs.CEntityReadFile -> recursiveReadFileEntity) is the exemplar.

phase2.target: BMS and FPac remain INDEPENDENT source/resource DSL pipelines. Their semantic generation migrates from the legacy reflective direct emitters onto declarative bindings + an appropriate recursive ST4 assembly contract, WITHOUT coupling their parsing or semantics to COBOL. Common rendering infrastructure (ST4 group files, the runtime contract, DiagnosticSink fail-closed behavior) is reused only where the semantic model genuinely supports it.

See discoveredDebt FPAC-LEGACY-SILENT-DROP and FPAC-GENERATOR-COUPLINGS; 2 dormant backends are deleted together with the pipeline.

phase2.completionCondition: Every production-reachable BMS/FPac ledger item is terminal (direct-retired/done); bmsDirectBackends and fpacDirectBackends are 0 with the checked-in Java inventory baselines tightened to 0; generated outputs compile where applicable; representative end-to-end behavior is preserved (BMS artifact contract green; FPac focused fixtures green); all prior COBOL/SQL/CICS gates stay green (directBackends frozen at 0, cloud-native gate green, online corpus inventory unchanged); the final architecture checks pass for all enabled scopes.

scheduler.note: Fields consumed by the external loop in tools/st4-loop (run-loop.sh). The loop is configured by migration PHASE (--phase): phase-1-cobol = COBOL_CORE/EMBEDDED_SQL/EMBEDDED_CICS (complete; kept replayable with its zero-debt gates); the active default phase-2-bms-fpac = BMS_ARTIFACT then FPAC. Within a phase the queue scopes are ORDERED: every READY item of an earlier scope is drained before any later scope (BMS fully before FPAC). Exactly one highest-priority READY item is selected per iteration and handed to one fresh worker. Per-entry fields: priority (lower=first), dependencies (ids that must be >= production-wired), verification (deterministic commands), expectedDebtDelta (per-scope counter: directBackends for COBOL scopes, bmsDirectBackends for BMS_ARTIFACT, fpacDirectBackends for FPAC), attempts, blocked, blockedReason, lastAttemptCommit. READY = scope in the phase queue, productionReachable, not terminal (status direct-retired or done -- debt already removed, never re-selected), not blocked, all dependencies satisfied.
scheduler.workerDefaults: permission-mode=acceptEdits (configurable via --permission-mode among acceptEdits/auto/plan/manual; bypassPermissions/dontAsk/dangerously-skip are refused), worker-timeout=1800s (configurable via --worker-timeout), prompt piped via stdin, git-mutation deny rules always applied. Claude API/quota errors pause the run without consuming ledger attempts or marking the semantic slice blocked.
